name: Issue resolution desk
description: A config-driven, repo-agnostic issue-resolution desk with a shared workflow sandbox across four phases — Advise (planner explores the issue and writes .desk/plan.md), Execute (implementer follows the plan, dedupes open PRs, fixes the issue, and waits for CI), Grade (reviewer grades the change, posts PR comments, and writes structured .desk/grade.json), and Dream (retrospective appends durable lessons to .desk/memory.md for the next round). A GitHub issue (bound to a task by the github sync) flows through pre-checks, then the advisor plans; if the plan flags NEEDS_HUMAN the desk pauses in the same run for a human plan review (TaskReviewCard) before Execute — the shared sandbox stays alive. Otherwise the implementer resolves the issue on a persistent workspace — adopting an existing open PR when one already resolves the issue, or opening tale/<id> — then the reviewer grades and a toolless LLM judge reads the structured grade to decide merge-readiness. Wrong approach sends the run back to Advise for a replan; approval parks at In review; otherwise Dream captures lessons and the desk loops Execute → Grade → Judge until the judge approves or the configurable rework cap (config.variables.maxReworkLoops, default 3) is reached. Cross-phase state lives in .desk/ on the shared workspace plus reworkCount in workflow variables. Every step carries ui/role annotations so the generic operator workspace renders it with no per-vertical UI code.

steps.name: Do we have the issue coordinates?

config.description: The pre-check needs owner/repo/issue_number to call get_issue. A task with a malformed or non-GitHub external ref (nothing parsed) skips straight to the normal flow, where the implementer derives the repo from the issue URL itself — so a bad ref never hard-fails the run.

If the issue is still open, run the normal resolve → review flow. If it is ALREADY closed (merged, fixed elsewhere, won't-fix, duplicate) there is nothing for the desk to do — skip the whole implement/review loop (saving the implementer + reviewer sandbox spend) and mark the task done.

steps.name: Implementer resolves the issue & opens/updates the PR

run.instructions:
Resolve this GitHub issue: '{{input.task.title}}' (#{{input.issueNumber}}) at {{input.task.externalUrl}}
{{input.task.description}}

Git is already authenticated for https (broker $GITHUB_TOKEN + credential helper), so commit/push work, private repos included.

REPO NOTES — operator-provided guidance for THIS repo from the app config (may be empty; when present, follow it): {{input.appConfig.repoNotes}}

SHARED WORKSPACE — this sandbox is the same workspace the advisor used. If `/user/workspace/.git` exists, do NOT re-clone; `cd /user/workspace`. Otherwise `cd /user/workspace && git clone <repo> .` (trailing `.` — repo root IS the workspace root). Export `OWNER` and `REPO`.

READ `.desk/plan.md` — your implementation MUST follow the advisor's plan (acceptance criteria, affected files, approach, test strategy). READ `.desk/state.json` for any branch/prNumber the advisor recorded; update it as you establish the canonical PR.

(1) DEDUPE BEFORE YOU BRANCH — never open a second PR for an issue that already has one. Enumerate the OPEN pull requests that resolve issue #{{input.issueNumber}}: (a) the ones GitHub has formally LINKED to it via a closing reference — `gh api graphql -F owner=$OWNER -F name=$REPO -F num={{input.issueNumber}} -f query='query($owner:String!,$name:String!,$num:Int!){repository(owner:$owner,name:$name){issue(number:$num){closedByPullRequestsReferences(first:50,includeClosedPrs:false){nodes{number headRefName url state isDraft author{login}}}}}}'`; (b) PLUS a text fallback for PRs that mention it without a formal link — `gh pr list --repo $OWNER/$REPO --state open --search '{{input.issueNumber}} in:title,body' --json number,headRefName,url,author,updatedAt` and any open `tale/*` head branch. Union the results, keep only OPEN PRs, and confirm by reading each candidate's title/body/diff that it truly targets THIS issue (discard a PR that only mentions #{{input.issueNumber}} in passing but fixes something else).

(2) PICK THE CANONICAL PR and set `BRANCH` (persist branch + prNumber in `.desk/state.json`):
  - If our branch `tale/{{input.task._id}}` already has an open PR -> that is canonical (the normal rework path); `BRANCH=tale/{{input.task._id}}`.
  - Else if exactly ONE other open PR resolves the issue -> ADOPT it: it is canonical and you commit your update onto ITS head branch; set `BRANCH` to that head ref. Do NOT open a competing PR.
  - Else if SEVERAL open PRs resolve the issue -> read each one's contents carefully (diff, tests, CI state, review comments, how complete the fix is) and choose the single furthest-along as canonical (prefer green/most-complete CI, the most thorough fix, one already under review); set `BRANCH` to its head ref. Then, for every OTHER duplicate that is genuinely redundant (same issue, superseded by the canonical one, not merged, carrying no unique work worth keeping), close it: `gh pr close <n> --repo $OWNER/$REPO --comment 'Superseded by #<canonical> — closing as a duplicate fix for issue #{{input.issueNumber}}.'`. Be conservative — closing is reversible, but only close CLEAR duplicates; never delete a human's branch, and if a PR holds distinct work the canonical one lacks, leave it open and flag it in your summary.
  - Else (NO open PR exists yet) -> `BRANCH=tale/{{input.task._id}}`; you will create it and open the PR in step 6.

(3) CHECK OUT THE WORKING BRANCH: `git fetch origin "$BRANCH" && git checkout "$BRANCH"`, or for a brand-new `tale/{{input.task._id}}` with no remote yet `git checkout -b "$BRANCH"`.

(4) IF THE CANONICAL PR ALREADY EXISTED this is a RE-WORK pass: the reviewer records what must change in `.desk/grade.json` and as comments on the PR, so act ONLY on feedback NEWER than the branch's current HEAD commit (earlier rounds were already handled by earlier commits). Get HEAD's time with `git log -1 --format=%cI`, then fetch the PR's review summaries, inline review comments, and issue comments (`gh pr view "$BRANCH" --repo $OWNER/$REPO --json reviews,comments` plus `gh api repos/$OWNER/$REPO/pulls/<number>/comments`) and treat only those submitted/created AFTER that HEAD timestamp as your to-do list; also read `.desk/grade.json` from the last Grade phase. Ignore older comments that predate HEAD.

(5) Implement or refine the fix per `.desk/plan.md`, then VERIFY IT YOURSELF — find the project's OWN test/build command from its config and run it until green. Operator-configured test command for THIS repo (when non-empty, use it as the test/build command): {{input.appConfig.testCommand}}

(6) COMMIT following the repo's convention (default Conventional Commits so a repo with commit-lint accepts it): `git add -A && git commit -m "fix: {{input.task.title}} (#{{input.issueNumber}})"` (lowercase type, no trailing period), then `git push -u origin "$BRANCH"`. If `$BRANCH` has NO PR yet, open one to the repo's default branch with a body that formally links the issue (include `Closes #{{input.issueNumber}}` so future runs find it via the link) via `gh pr create` or the GitHub REST API with $GITHUB_TOKEN — otherwise your push already updated the canonical PR. Update `.desk/state.json` with the final branch and prNumber.

(7) WAIT FOR CI: once the PR exists, watch its checks with `gh pr checks "$BRANCH" --repo $OWNER/$REPO --watch` (or poll `gh pr checks "$BRANCH" --repo $OWNER/$REPO`) until they ALL finish. If any check FAILS, read its logs (`gh run view --log-failed`, or open the failing run), fix the cause, commit, push (the PR + checks re-run), and watch again — repeat until every required check is green. If the FAILING check is a commit-message / commit-lint check, the fix is NOT a new commit — AMEND the message to the repo's required convention (e.g. `git commit --amend -m "fix: ..."`) and force-push with `git push --force-with-lease origin "$BRANCH"`. Do NOT finish with red or still-pending CI. CI can take 40+ minutes; that is expected — keep waiting, this step is durable and will not time out mid-watch.

MANDATORY: write `.desk/implement-log.md` (what you changed, canonical PR, CI state, rework context) and `/user/output/summary.md` covering what you changed, the canonical PR number + URL, any duplicate PRs you closed and why (or chose to leave open and why), the checks/tests you ran, the FINAL CI state (which checks passed), and the PR URL.

config.description: A sandbox step always returns the success port; the real verdict is in output.data.ok. Stop if the implementer failed to push a verified fix + PR.

steps.name: Reviewer grades the change & comments on the PR

run.instructions:
Grade the implementer's fix for '{{input.task.title}}' (#{{input.issueNumber}}) at {{input.task.externalUrl}}. Git is authenticated ($GITHUB_TOKEN + helper). REPO NOTES — operator-provided guidance for THIS repo from the app config (may be empty; when present, weigh it in your review): {{input.appConfig.repoNotes}}

SHARED WORKSPACE — do NOT re-clone; the repo is already at `/user/workspace` from earlier phases. `cd /user/workspace` and export `OWNER` and `REPO` from the remote or `.desk/state.json`.

READ `.desk/plan.md` for acceptance criteria and the grade schema the advisor defined. READ `.desk/state.json` to resolve the canonical PR/branch the implementer worked on.

RESOLVE THE CANONICAL PR — the single OPEN pull request that resolves issue #{{input.issueNumber}} (use branch/prNumber from `.desk/state.json` when set; otherwise find via `gh api graphql` / `gh pr list` as in the implementer dedupe flow). Set `BRANCH` to its head ref, then `git fetch origin "$BRANCH" && git checkout "$BRANCH"`.

READ THE CHANGE — `git fetch origin main && git diff origin/main...HEAD` (or the repo's default branch instead of `main` when that is not default). Understand the full diff in context of the plan.

RUN TESTS ONCE — operator-configured test command for THIS repo (use when non-empty): {{input.appConfig.testCommand}}. Confirm CI with `gh pr checks "$BRANCH" --repo $OWNER/$REPO` — red OR still-pending CI is a BLOCKING problem.

REVIEW BY YOUR FULL METHOD — do NOT collapse this into one linear sweep, and ALWAYS run BOTH rounds: ROUND 1 (breadth) dispatching 5–30 parallel review subagents SIZED TO THE ACTUAL CHANGE (≈5 for a small focused PR, scaling up toward 30 as the changed files / logic branches / modules grow — never fewer than 5, never more than 30), then ROUND 2 (confirmation) independently re-verifying every finding you would block the merge on.

REPORT — post your review as comments on the pull request (`gh pr review` / `gh pr comment`, or the GitHub REST API with $GITHUB_TOKEN) — do NOT change or push code.

MANDATORY STRUCTURED OUTPUT — write BOTH `.desk/grade.json` AND `/user/output/grade.json` (identical content) using the schema/fields the advisor specified in `.desk/plan.md` (include severity, verdict-ready signal, blocking findings, CI state, test outcome). Also write `/user/output/summary.md`: state the CI state (which checks passed/failed) and clearly whether the change is ready to merge or what specifically must be fixed.

config.name: merge-judge
config.systemPrompt:
You are a strict merge gate for a code-review desk. You are given ONLY the reviewer's structured grade JSON for a proposed fix. Decide merge-readiness from it alone — you have no tools and no other context. Reply with EXACTLY two lines and nothing else:
severity: merge_ready|minor_fix|major_rework|wrong_approach
verdict: yes|no

Use severity merge_ready only when the grade reports no blocking problems and CI/tests are green. Use wrong_approach when the fundamental approach is unsound and replanning is needed. Use minor_fix or major_rework with verdict no when more implementation work is required. Use verdict yes only for merge_ready severity.

config.description: When the judge's severity is wrong_approach, the desk sends the run back to Advise for a fresh plan instead of looping Execute with the same approach.

The judge replies with a bare yes/no verdict line (trimmed); jexl `in` does substring, and a 'no' can never contain 'yes', so this never false-approves. If yes, park for human merge; otherwise route through Dream and the rework counter.

run.instructions:
The judge ruled wrong_approach for issue #{{input.issueNumber}} ('{{input.task.title}}'). Rework loops so far: {{variables.reworkCount || 0}}/{{config.maxReworkLoops}}.

Read all files under `/user/workspace/.desk/`. Append durable lessons to `.desk/memory.md` about why the approach failed and what to avoid next round. Write `/user/output/summary.md` listing what you appended.

The judge approved the change for issue #{{input.issueNumber}} ('{{input.task.title}}'). Rework loops: {{variables.reworkCount || 0}}/{{config.maxReworkLoops}}.

Read all files under `/user/workspace/.desk/`. Append durable lessons to `.desk/memory.md` — what worked, repo traps, CI quirks worth remembering. Write `/user/output/summary.md` listing what you appended.

The judge sent the change back for more work on issue #{{input.issueNumber}} ('{{input.task.title}}'). Rework loops so far: {{variables.reworkCount || 0}}/{{config.maxReworkLoops}}.

Read all files under `/user/workspace/.desk/` (especially grade.json). Append durable lessons to `.desk/memory.md` about what failed review and patterns to fix. Write `/user/output/summary.md` listing what you appended.

steps.name: Log the merge-ready verdict on the task

parameters.body: [automated] 🎯 The desk reviewed and approved this change — the pull request is ready for a human to merge. Rework loops: {{variables.reworkCount || 0}}/{{config.maxReworkLoops}}.{{(variables.reworkCount || 0) == 0 ? ' First-pass approval.' : ''}}

config.description: Bounds the grade → execute rework loop. reworkCount (workflow variables) counts how many times the reviewer has sent the change back; allow up to config.variables.maxReworkLoops reworks (default 3, adjustable per deployment). While within budget, loop back to the implementer with the latest feedback; once exhausted, escalate to a human instead of looping until the workflow timeout.

steps.name: Rework limit reached — escalate to a human

parameters.body: [automated] The desk reached its rework limit ({{config.maxReworkLoops}} loops; used {{variables.reworkCount}}) without the reviewer approving the change. The pull request is left open with the latest attempt and the review feedback — a human should take it over from here. Moving to In review.
